ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the picture, a tall and massive Mount Fuji can be seen, with the summit covered in white snow, and the foreground and both sides framed by blooming flower branches, matching the characteristics of a Mount Fuji photograph of “cherry blossoms blooming below the mountain and white snow gleaming on the mountain.” Reasoning: The question stem states that Mount Fuji is located about 100 km west of the Keihin area. The area most affected by volcanic ash is usually the downwind area of the volcano. In winter, prevailing westerly winds and northwesterly winds prevail in Japan; the wind blows from the western side where Mount Fuji is located toward the eastern side or southeastern side. The Keihin area is located near the eastern side of Mount Fuji, so in winter volcanic ash is most easily transported to the Keihin area, and the impact is greatest.

raw_record.question_text: Mount Fuji is an active volcano, and volcanic ash has a great impact on the Keihin area. If Mount Fuji has a volcanic eruption, in which season would the impact on the Keihin area be the greatest?

method.method_draft: Describe the image as a photo of snow-capped Mount Fuji framed by blossoms, then read the prompt for the key spatial relation: Fuji is about 100 km west of the Keihin region. Apply the ash-transport rule: the region most affected is the one downwind of the volcano. Compare seasons by Japan’s prevailing winds; in winter, northwesterly/westerly winds blow from Fuji’s side toward the east/southeast where Keihin is located. Therefore the season with the greatest impact is winter.
